# Draft:Battle of Kairouan

Battle of Kairouan (1053), was a conflict between the population of Kairouan and the Banu Hilal tribe. It occurred after the Hilalians were permitted to enter the city, but a tense atmosphere eventually led to open fighting.
The Battle
After the defeat at al-Musalla, the situation calmed for a short period. In 1053, al-Muʿizz built walls around Kairouan and Zuwaylah to protect the city. At the same time, he sought to end the war between him and the Arab tribes and to make peace with them. To achieve this, he allowed them to enter the city for trade. Hadi R. Idris noted that the scholars of Kairouan were angered by these trade activities, as such transactions were considered forbidden, since the Hilalians' money, crops, and other possessions had been obtained through plunder.
It was not long before quarrels broke out between the local population and the Hilalians, who were said to behave with arrogance, rudeness, and harshness. A dispute between a local inhabitant and a Bedouin escalated into a large-scale battle between Banu Hilal and the people of Kairouan. The Arabs emerged victorious, while the people of Kairouan were defeated and massacred. It is unknown how or when the Arabs later left the city.
Aftermath
The experiment undertaken by al-Muʿizz without sufficient caution ended in heavy losses. His relationship with Banu Hilal was afterward limited primarily to marital alliances, as he married his daughters to some of their leaders. These leaders later escorted him to Mahdia, before Kairouan was sacked in 1057.
